title: Meridian Logistics — Q4 results summary
note: Constructed, not real. Written so that a substantial number of clauses invert in valence between a credit and an equity mandate — leverage taken on to fund a buyback, growth bought with margin, a covenant amendment, deteriorating cash conversion, and rising customer concentration. Using a constructed note makes the effect legible and sidesteps licensing; it also makes the effect larger than it would be on an arbitrary document, which is recorded in docs/calibration.md section 6.7.
texts: Meridian Logistics reported fourth-quarter revenue of $1.42bn, up 19% year on year.
This is the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit top-line growth.
Growth was led by the Freight Solutions segment, which grew 31%.
Gross margin declined 240 basis points to 22.1%.
Management attributes the margin decline to onboarding costs on new enterprise contracts.
Adjusted EBITDA of $196m was broadly flat against the prior year.
The adjustment adds back $34m of transformation costs, the third consecutive year such costs have been described as non-recurring.
Operating cash flow fell to $88m from $141m.
Days sales outstanding extended from 47 days to 63 days.
The company noted it has offered extended payment terms to secure several large contracts.
Net debt rose to $2.1bn following the acquisition of Kestrel Freight in October.
Net leverage stands at 4.1x adjusted EBITDA, against 2.9x a year ago.
In November the company agreed an amendment with its lending syndicate, raising the maximum permitted leverage covenant from 4.0x to 4.75x through to December 2027.
The amendment carries a 75 basis point increase in margin on the term loan.
The board approved a $300m share repurchase programme, to be funded from the revolving credit facility.
The quarterly dividend was raised 8% to 27 cents.
The company's three largest customers now represent 41% of group revenue, up from 29%.
The largest of these contracts is due for renewal in the second half of 2027.
Management described the renewal pipeline as constructive.
$1.4bn of the term loan matures in March 2028.
The company holds $210m of cash and has $340m undrawn on its revolving credit facility.
Kestrel Freight contributed $61m of revenue in the quarter.
Kestrel is expected to deliver $40m of annual run-rate synergies by 2028, raised from $28m at the time of announcement.
Integration is described as ahead of schedule.
Headcount reduced by 4% during the quarter.
The company opened its automated hub in Rotterdam, its largest capital project to date.
Capital expenditure guidance for next year was reduced from $240m to $185m.
Management reiterated full-year guidance of 15 to 17% revenue growth.
The Chief Financial Officer announced she will step down in March, after six years in the role.
A successor has not yet been named.
relevance_note: Author-assigned, applying each persona's stated mandate to each clause. Deliberately independent of the model's scoring, so the L1 check in cmp.targets is a genuine external test rather than a restatement of the model's own output. These masks are a judgment, not a measurement. IMPORTANT: 'relevant' here means the minority of clauses this role would actually fixate on — the ones that drive the decision — not every clause that bears on the mandate. The first draft used the looser reading and marked 17 of 30 clauses relevant for the credit analyst; a majority mask makes the suppression-asymmetry constraint vacuous under a fixed attention budget (see docs/calibration.md section 2), and it also misreads the literature, whose 'task-relevant areas' are always a minority of the display.
